name: JLT Runners
about: Dawn runs around JLT, the Marina walk and Jumeirah. Pace groups, heat-safe routes, shoe swaps and honest race recaps.

stories.author: p02
stories.text: 5am group run along the lake, 8k done, the sky was pink. Who's joining Sunday?

stories.author: p10
stories.text: Swim and run combo this week. Fins for the sea, shoes for the sand. Yalla!

stories.author: p04
stories.text: New cycling-to-run loop from Business Bay to the canal. Smooth tarmac, few cars.

posts.author: p02
posts.text: Sunday dawn group run, meeting at the JLT lake gate at 5:15am. Pace groups: 5:30, 6:00 and 'chatty pace'. Bring water, the heat is coming early this year.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Chatty pace is my natural habitat. Count me in with the pancakes after.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Can I bring my puppy? He sprints faster than most of us, I promise.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: 5:15 is a spiritual hour for me. I'll be there with the playlist and a tired smile.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Cycling pace group would be great too, I can do slow laps around the lake.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee truck near the gate after 6am would be perfect, just saying.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: First time in a group run. Is it beginner friendly for someone who runs 3k on a good day?

comments.author: p10
comments.text: @hannah_b yes, the chatty pace group has walk breaks. Nobody gets left behind.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Pancakes after a run is a sacred ritual. Bring a box of cupcakes too, I'll bake.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Will there be a route with shade? Last Sunday's run was brutal in the sun.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: @anjali_rao yes, the lake loop has trees on the north side, cooler and nicer.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Trees on the north side, got it. Water bottle, sunscreen, let's go.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Heat index is high this week, carry electrolytes not just water. Safer for everyone.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Great advice Tomasz. Pup gets water too, we're a team of hydration freaks.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Heard the lake path closes for maintenance some mornings. Check the notice first.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I will be the one who sprints for the coffee at the end, don't wait for me.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Adding this to my calendar. Thank you for making the run social, it helps a lot.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Post run stretching by the water, five minutes, no excuses. Coach's orders.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I'll bring the cupcakes in a box that survives the run. Wish me luck.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @omar_q the coach has spoken. Stretching is a must, I learned that the painful way.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks all, see you Sunday at the gate. Keep the energy up, the sun is no joke.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Chatty pace group gets a team name? Suggestions: the Slow Lap Crew.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: The Slow Lap Crew has a great ring to it. Playlist name: Slow Jams.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approves the team name. He has already started barking the rhythm.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Cycling version: the Fast Spokes, to balance out the Slow Lap Crew.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Can we get a group photo at the end? I want to remember my first group run.

posts.author: p10
posts.text: Swim and run training is my favourite combo. Two laps in the sea, then a 4k run on the beach. My legs feel light and the sand is brutal in the best way.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Sand runs are underrated. Your calves will hate you for a week, then love you forever.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Sea swims before a run feel like a cheat code. Cold water recovers my legs too.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Coach, what's the pace on the sand? I'm too scared to ask but I want to try.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: @sarak start slow, sand is four times harder than road. Walk when you need to.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Sand plus sunscreen plus a hot run equals a sticky mess. Worth it though.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy wants to join the sand run. He ran two metres and then decided the sea is better.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: The beach at sunrise with a swim is a Dubai luxury people don't appreciate enough.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'm a coffee-first person, so the swim is a bold move before caffeine. Respect.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Do you swim with a wetsuit in summer or just the shorts? Asking for a friend.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: @hannah_b in summer just shorts. In winter a light wetsuit, the water is still warm.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: I'd need a lifeguard, a towel and a snack bag for this. Very impressed.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Post-swim run means salt on the skin, so bring a fresh shirt. Chafing is the enemy.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good tip. Also use a bit of body glide, the salt water makes it worse.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Body glide, fresh shirt, sunscreen, got my list ready for Saturday.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy needs his own swim plan. Maybe a separate beach day with the vet nurses.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Music on the beach run is a must. Bring headphones, not a speaker, be considerate.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Post-run espresso on the sand is my idea of heaven. I'll be the guy with the thermos.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Can I come as a spectator? I'll bring coffee for the finishers.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Coffee for finishers, and cake too? Sounds like a plan to me.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Yes, coffee and cake and a stretching circle. That's my recovery plan.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Sand run on Saturday, I'll join with the chatty pace group. Yalla.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Lifeguard check: is the beach patrolled at 6am? Safety first, please.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: @anjali_rao yes, the patrol starts at 6am on the main beach. Always swim in the flagged zone.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good, safety comes first. Thanks Omar for keeping the group sane.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: This thread convinced me. Sand, sea and sunrise, I'm in next week.

posts.author: p04
posts.text: New cycling-to-run loop from Business Bay to the Dubai Water Canal, then back via the bridge. About 16km total, smooth tarmac, few cars, shade on the north bank.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Shade on the north bank is the detail I needed. Adding it to my weekend plan.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'd add a coffee stop at the midpoint, the canal views are worth a slow sip.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: 16km is my long run now. Thanks for mapping it, Tomasz, the route saves me a lot of thinking.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Music on the bridge at sunset is a whole vibe. Bring the speaker, but keep it low.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy-friendly? I need a loop with a water bowl near the start line.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Is there a bike rack near the start? Want to bring my bike and run back.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: @hannah_b there is a rack by the metro entrance, arrive early, it fills up.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Canal side in the morning is gorgeous. The water reflects the towers, lovely light.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: The loop passes my favourite bakery. Dangerous but motivating, honestly.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Is there a water fountain halfway? I always run out around the eighth km.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Yes, a small fountain near the bridge, it works most mornings, not guaranteed.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Carry a bottle regardless. Fountains in Dubai are a gamble, learnt that the hard way.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Hydration tip from a coffee man: a cold brew after the run is the reward.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Cold water in the face at the canal, the best trick of summer training.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Pups need water too, so the fountain question is serious for me.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: The loop is perfect for a weekend bike and run combo. Thanks for sharing.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Let's do a group ride-and-run on this loop next month. Who's in?

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Yes! I'll bring the sunscreen and the good playlist, you bring the bike.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Ride and run and cake at the end. Honestly that's my dream sport.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Count me in if we start after 6am, before the heat hits the canal.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: 6am is the sweet spot. Maybe 5:45 for the real runners.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Route map link to follow in the group, no external links on this thread though.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good call, keep the links in the group chat, not here. Ready for the loop.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Fine, I'll bring the thermos. Let's hit the canal together soon.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Canal crew confirmed. Yalla, legs are warming up already.

posts.author: p07
posts.text: Ran my first 10k without stopping, in June heat, at 5:30am in Mirdif. I still cannot believe it. Thank you to this group for the tips on pacing and hydration.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Huge congrats Anjali! That's a serious milestone, the first 10k feels like a mountain.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Congrats! The puppy is jumping around in celebration, I can hear him from here.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Proud of you. Pacing is everything, you clearly listened. Well done.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Congratulations! I'm making you a cake shaped like a running shoe, no arguments.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Amazing effort! What was your pace? I'm trying to get under six minutes soon.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: In June heat that's a huge win. Mirdif loop is hilly in the middle, respect.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: You should have a playlist for the last two kilometres, trust me, it helps.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'll buy you a celebratory flat white after the next group run, it's the least I can do.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Inspiring. I'm still at the 3k stage, your story gives me hope.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @hannah_b everyone starts at 3k. Keep going, you'll be surprised how fast it builds.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: The first 10k is a mental game more than physical. Glad you cracked it.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Did you take a salt tablet? Heat plus long distance needs more than water.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @omar_q yes, a salt tablet at 6k and electrolytes at the start. Good call.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Electrolytes and a banana, my old formula. Works every time for me.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: The puppy wants to know if there will be a treat at the finish line. Please say yes.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Huge milestone and the group is proud. Keep posting the progress, it inspires.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Let's celebrate with a brunch after the Sunday run, Anjali's treat, everyone's invited.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Brunch means cake. That's the rule. I'll bring the shoe cake.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Shoe cake and a coffee, that's the best finish line I've heard of.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: What shoes did you use? I need to upgrade mine before the next race.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @hannah_b my trainers are the basic model. Fit matters more than the brand, get a proper gait check.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: A gait check at a running store is worth it. Half the pain is bad shoes.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good shoes plus good sunscreen plus good company. The three things that make a run.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approved your 10k with a happy tail wag. From him, that's a gold medal.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Keep the streak going, Anjali. The next target is 15k, we'll be there cheering.

posts.author: p06
posts.text: Honest question about recovery: how many rest days per week do you take? I'm doing five runs and wondering if I'm pushing too hard in this heat. Advice welcome 🎧

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Two proper rest days, one of them with swimming or stretching only. Your body needs the break.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Five runs in summer heat is a lot. I'd drop to four and keep the long one on Sunday.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Watch your resting heart rate. If it climbs three days in a row, take a full rest day.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I'm no runner, but rest days are a must for any hobby. Bakers need them too.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Sleep is the real recovery, not the rest day. Eight hours and you feel new.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: My puppy takes two naps and a rest day every week. Maybe we are learning from him.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: I push too hard when I feel good. A rest day saves me from injuries, I learnt slowly.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee doesn't count as recovery, I'm told. Sorry, I still tried.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: What about cross training? Cycling a few times a week instead of running?

comments.author: p04
comments.text: @hannah_b yes, cycling is brilliant cross training, low impact and it keeps the legs moving.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Swimming is the best low-impact recovery, I'd say. Add it on the rest day.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Thanks all, very helpful. I'll cut to four runs and add a swim on Wednesday.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Good plan. Also drink more water on the rest days, your muscles repair with fluids.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Stretch before bed, five minutes. My calves thank me every morning.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Foam roller plus a warm bath plus a cake, that's my recovery routine.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: If the knee hurts for more than a few days, see a physio. Please don't ignore it.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Agreed, pain is information. Listen, rest, come back stronger.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'd add a light walk on rest days, a stroll gets the blood moving without stress.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: I'm starting a training log this week. Rest days included, I promise to log them.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Logging rest days is a brilliant habit. Half of training is knowing when to stop.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Heat acclimatisation takes about two weeks, so ease in if you're new to the summer.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Two weeks of easy runs, then add the intensity. Patience pays off in Dubai.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Patience, rest and a good playlist. My new training motto. Thank you all 🎶

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy says rest is his favourite part of the training plan. Honest dog.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good luck with the four-run plan Kwame, report back after two weeks.

posts.author: p09
posts.text: Shoe swap week in the group! Share the pair you love, the one you hate, and the price you paid. I'll start: my lightweight racers, 480 AED, not worth it for daily runs.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: I run daily in the cushioned pair, 520 AED. Worth it for long runs, boring for everything else.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Swim shoes and sandals are my two pairs. Sandals on the beach, always, sand loves to hide in trainers.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Basic budget trainers from the mall, 220 AED. They've lasted two years, no complaints.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Cycling shoes clip in, so the running pair is separate. Shoe cupboard is getting full.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: I buy trainers for the puppy's walks, but the dog eats my old pairs. Don't leave shoes out.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: My pair hurts my heel after 10k, is that normal? Shopping for a new fit soon.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Heel pain usually means the drop or cushioning is wrong. Get a gait check, I'm serious.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: I'm loyal to one brand for years, but the new model feels off. Shoe loyalty is complicated.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Shoes are like coffee beans, the best one is the one that fits your routine.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: @sarak the gait check at the running store is free in some places, call ahead.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Trail shoes are another category, though we don't have many trails here. Sand is the trail.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Sand is the trail, true. Lightweight trainers handle sand best, the heavy ones sink.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Socks matter too. Moisture wicking socks changed my life, and they're cheap.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good socks and good shoes plus good sunscreen, the holy trinity again, lol.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's favourite shoe is the one left on the balcony. Please, nobody leave them out.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Thanks all, I'll try the gait check on Saturday before the group run.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Share your shoe size and the brand you like, we can do a bulk discount run.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I'll bring a box of cupcakes for the shoe swap, a sweet bribe for the swap.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee is the better swap. Shoes you trade, coffee you share.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep the swap in the group, not in the comments, the thread is getting busy.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Fair point, Omar. Next thread will be a proper shoe swap event.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Great energy in this thread. The shoe swap is officially on for next Sunday.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Cycling and running in one group is a good mix, the group gets better each week.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy submitted his paw measurements for the shoe swap. He's serious about it.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Count me in for the swap. I'll bring the mall pair and a lot of enthusiasm.

posts.author: p03
posts.text: Post-run snack ideas that won't ruin your stomach? Trying to find something sweet but light after a 12k run in this heat, bakery treats are not an option this time.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Banana with peanut butter. Simple, cheap and the carbs refill you fast.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Dates and yoghurt. Sweet, light, and my grandmother swore by it after work.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Chilled watermelon after the sea swim, the best post-run snack. Hydrates too.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Oats with honey and berries, prepared the night before. Fast and light.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's post-run snack is a carrot. I'm trying it myself, it's surprisingly good.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Chocolate milk, the classic. Protein and sugar, the recovery drink that works.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Mango with a pinch of salt, the Mirdif summer favourite. Sweet and refreshing.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee plus dates. Yes, I'm the guy who does that after every run.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Greek yoghurt with honey and nuts, I eat it straight from the fridge.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Thank you all, I'll try the dates and yoghurt combo this week, sounds lovely.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: @layla_h add a few walnuts, the crunch makes the snack feel like a treat.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Peanut butter on rice cakes is my cheat snack when the sweet craving hits.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep it light, the stomach can cramp after heavy snacks in the heat. Learned that hard.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: The puppy got a bite of banana and loved it. Dogs know good food.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Smoothie with frozen fruit and oats, super cold, super easy, very Dubai summer.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: A proper recovery shake with milk, banana and cocoa. Tastes like dessert.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Dates stuffed with almonds, the desert-style treat that works for runners.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Please add espresso to the recovery list, it's a scientific must in my book.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Greek yoghurt bowl with fruit is what I do after every long run. Simple and filling.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Adding this whole list to the recipe book. Thanks everyone, you've saved my weekend.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Don't forget the fluids, electrolytes in the first hour. The snack is the second step.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Coconut water is my go-to. Sweet, salty, and no fuss.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Coconut water plus a fresh mango is the perfect beach run finish, trust the coach.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy wants you to know he is still waiting for that banana, Omar.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good snack list. Everyone should try the dates and yoghurt at least once.

posts.author: p04
posts.text: Heat safety reminder for the group: if you feel dizzy, cold, or stop sweating, stop, sit in shade, and get help. Early summer heat is not a joke here, please look after each other.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Very important. Shade, water, and a buddy. No hero runs in July, ever.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks for posting this. I had a near miss last summer, a cold shower saved me.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy and I are staying indoors after eight. The asphalt is too hot for paws.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Carry a small first aid kit with electrolytes. Better safe than sorry on long routes.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Run with a buddy, always. The app tracks your route, but a friend knows when to call.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Keep your phone charged and share your route before you leave. Simple habits.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Heat stroke is serious. If someone is confused, call emergency help immediately.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee doesn't help heat stress, water does. Lesson learned from my own sweaty mornings.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our group should add a heat policy to the pinned post. Clear rules keep everyone safe.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good idea Hannah. I'll draft a short version and pin it, one page, no fluff.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Lifeguards on the beach can help too, if you're near the sea just ask for water.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Early morning runs are safest. Aim to finish before 7am in summer, no exceptions.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's rule: if the ground is too hot for your hand, it's too hot for paws.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Hand on the pavement test, I love it. Adding it to my routine right now.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Music at a lower volume so you can hear traffic and people. Safety first on the road.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Thank you for this reminder, I almost ran in the afternoon last week. Never again.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Let's keep this thread as a reminder. Share your own heat tips below, please.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Stop for water at the coffee stand, the staff there are very helpful, I promise.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Take a cooling towel. They are cheap and they make a huge difference in the heat.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Ice in a cap and cold water on the neck, the tricks my coach taught me.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Heat plus salt plus water, always. A balanced approach keeps you running all summer.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Stay safe everyone, see you at the gate in the early light. Yalla, we run smart.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy is now officially the group's heat safety mascot. He wears his cooling vest.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Thank you, Tomasz, for keeping the group sensible. Respect.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Stay cool, stay hydrated, and take care of the buddy next to you 🎧

posts.author: p01
posts.text: Ran past the new art murals near Al Quoz this morning and felt like I was in a different city. Anyone want a Saturday route that ends at a cafe with proper shade?

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Al Quoz murals are great. The cafe near the tyre warehouse has shaded seats, come by after.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Saturday works for me. I'll bring the route plan and the sunscreen, you bring the smile.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Art and running is a perfect weekend mix. I'll add a bike ride before it for a cross session.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Shaded cafe after a run is the best reward, I'm in if the water is cold.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy-friendly cafe? He wants to see the murals too, he's very into art.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Art, run and coffee. That's a three-part Saturday I can get behind.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Where do you park? Al Quoz parking is tricky, I always end up circling the block.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Metro plus a short walk, it's easier than parking. Trust me on that one.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I'll bring cake to the cafe, the bakers' code says sharing is caring.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Route is about 9km with two murals on the way. The Saturday pace is relaxed.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Nine kilometres with photo stops, that's my kind of run. Let's go.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Sun is strong at 7am now, so meet at 6, before the heat builds.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: 6am is a fine time for me, coffee at 6:30 and the murals at 7. Perfect plan.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Who wants to see the sculpture near the warehouse? Best one on the route.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's vote goes to the big mural with the dogs painted on it. Very fitting.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Music at the murals is a nice idea. Quiet playlist, let's not disturb the artists.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Count me in. I want to take photos for the group album, I'm getting into photography.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Photographers and runners, a new combo. The album will be great.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Are there benches in case we need a sit-down? Cake bribery requires a seat.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Benches are there near the cafe, and the shade is generous. Don't worry, cake is safe.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Looking forward to Saturday. Please share your timing so we can plan the groups.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: I'll be on the bike, so my timing is flexible. Meet you at the cafe.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: The cafe has cold brew on tap, so bring thirst and good vibes.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Swim after the cafe if anyone wants to finish at the beach. Optional, obviously.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy will need a nap after the murals. Plan accordingly, friends 🐶

posts.author: p05
posts.text: Dog runners, a question: is it okay to run with a dog on the lake path in the morning? My puppy has so much energy and I want to share the routine with him.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Yes, with a leash and water. The lake path is quiet before 6am, perfect for a young pup.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Start with short runs, a young dog's joints are still growing. Walk breaks are a must.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Check the local rules on dogs in parks. Carry bags and pick up after him, always.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Heat is the real issue, so only mornings. Test the ground with your hand first.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: My dog runs with me every Sunday. Best training partner, never complains about the early start.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Puppy gets a biscuit at the end of each lap. Motivation is the secret, I'm told.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Get a harness, not a collar, for running. Much safer for the neck.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee break for the human while the dog sniffs every bush. Balance is important.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our dog ran a 5k with us last month. She slept all afternoon and then all night.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Thank you all. I'll start with a short walk-run combo and build up slowly.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Good plan. Keep the leash short near other joggers, not everyone likes dogs close.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Water bowl at the start and end of the run, the dog needs it more than you do.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Puppy is very lucky to have a runner, the lake path is a dream for dogs.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Keep the run calm, no sudden stops, and reward good behaviour. Simple rules.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Also watch for the other dogs on the path, some are nervous. Give them space.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: The puppy with a running bib would be the cutest thing on the lake, I'm sure.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Ask the vet nurse for a checkup before any long run, growing dogs need the all-clear.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'll watch out for your puppy when I'm walking the coffee cart, don't worry.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: What about winter? Is the lake path good for dogs in cooler months too?

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Winter is the best time for dog runs here, cool air and happy dogs.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Winter swims with a dog are a whole new level, just be sure the water is safe.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good luck, Mariam, I'm sure the pup will be a star on the lake path.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Thanks, everyone, this was really helpful. Puppy is already wagging his tail at the leash.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Let's see the first run photo next Sunday, the lake will be proud. 🎶

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Go Mariam and puppy! Tag us all in the photo, the group wants to see.
